articles.summary: arXiv:2610.31875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Technology tools used for professional upskilling change on a timescale of weeks, and written guidance about them ages at the same pace. articles.title: AusClinBench: a deterministically scored benchmark of large language models against current Australian clinical policy
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.31993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI models already inform clinical decisions and draft notes in Australian clinical software, usually without the practitioner being told which model is used. Existing medical benchmarks are written for other jurisdictions. We wrote 142 questions from Australian guidelines and schedules across five domains (PBS authority, MBS billing, Ahpra obligations, triage red flags, immunisation and screening), each with one verifiable answer scored by exact match. articles.title: Thumb on the scale: Using traditional wargaming adjudication practices to improve AI-judged evaluations and grading
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.32066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-ended AI work has no single correct answer to check, so a judge, often another AI, decides each result. Research on these judges asks which AI to use and how to word the rubric. It rarely tests the procedure that the judge follows. Wargames have no correct answer either, and for two centuries the field has designed that procedure: named methods that set how much freedom the referee has, their known failures, and fixes. articles.summary: arXiv:2610.32159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) systems do not merely render prompts; they circulate defaults for "what X looks like," shaping recognition through pose, camera, costume, props, and setting. articles.title: Democratic Accountability for Autonomous Systems: A Legislative Notification Framework and Comparative Institutional Design
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.32226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: No domestic legislature has ever reviewed a state's decision to authorise an autonomous cyber weapon before it acted. Closing the international attribution gap is necessary but not sufficient for democratic accountability. We formalise the Tripartite Attribution Framework's three attribution levels and add a fourth, non-legal Democratic Accountability level ($A_{dem}$): a 72-hour legislative notification requirement. articles.summary: arXiv:2610.32479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-area accessibility analysis remains difficult to reproduce because multimodal routing, heterogeneous opportunity data, and reusable spatial outputs are rarely integrated in a single transparent workflow. articles.summary: arXiv:2610.32576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data protection legislation aims to protect privacy rights by regulating how information systems store and process personal information.
